_comment: Dual-execution mock-fidelity corpus (ADR 0049, T6). Each journey is replayed against BOTH the TS mock runtime (src/test/scenarios/fidelity.test.ts) and the real Rust AppState/storage layer (src-tauri/src/storage/tests/mock_fidelity.rs). Both must satisfy every assertion, so the hand-written mock runtime cannot silently drift from real backend behavior (ts-rs guarantees DTO shapes; this guarantees behavior). Journeys use only seed-free root entities (watchlists, companies) so no scenario seeding is needed; assertions are seed-independent (create/rename/delete then assert the effect, never absolute counts), and a created entity's id is captured and reused so the assertions hold regardless of each side's id-derivation scheme. Step grammar: command, input (the invoke args, with "$name" leaves substituted from captures), optional capture (stores result.id), expectField (result object superset), expectContains / expectAbsent (result array contains / does not contain an element matching the subset).

fundamentals coverage assembles a period row from a fact (ADR 0077 T2.1)
journeys._comment: Coverage is a computed read model returning an object (companyId + periods array), not an array, so the subset harness can only assert its invariant top-level field. expectField is NOT capture-substituted (only step input is), so the companyId is asserted as the deterministic derived id (company_{exchange}_{ticker}, identical on both sides — the same scheme the qualified-ticker journey relies on). Per-cell correctness — a period row with facts.total >= 1 and report null — is pinned by the Rust unit tests and the TS mock scenario tests; this step proves both dispatchers implement the command and key the DTO by the scoped company.

journeys.name: flagged extraction outcomes read back as an empty array for a never-attempted company (ADR 0061 dec. 2)
journeys._comment: Outcome rows are written only by the extraction pipeline, whose tiers read stored report files (seeded through the network-bound fetch/backfill path, same rationale as the coverage step above). So the corpus pins the state that carries the guarantee: absence of a row means NEVER ATTEMPTED, and a fresh company therefore reads back an array with nothing in it — the honest "nothing flagged" state the UI must render as reassurance, never as a failure. expectAbsent asserts both that the result IS an array (so both dispatchers implement the command and return the read model, not an object or an error) and that no row names this company. Per-row correctness (typed reasonCode, sentinel period, in-place re-run) is pinned by the Rust unit tests and the TS panel tests.

journeys.name: flagged facts read back as an empty array for a company whose values all passed (epic #229 T5)
journeys._comment: The flagged-FACTS read (list_flagged_fact_provenance) gained a company scope and the fact context the Coverage panel renders. Provenance rows are written only by the extraction pipeline (network-bound stored files, same rationale as the coverage step above), so the corpus pins the shape both dispatchers must agree on: a company whose facts carry no flagged provenance reads back an ARRAY with no row naming it — never an object, never an error, and never another company's flagged figures leaking into a company-scoped read. Per-row enrichment (metric/label/value/period join) is pinned by the Rust store tests and the TS panel tests.

journeys.name: report documents view returns an empty rows array for a company with no documents (ADR 0077 Panel B)
journeys._comment: The view is a computed read model returning an object (companyId + rows array). Report documents are seeded only through the network-bound fetch/backfill path (same rationale as the T2.1 coverage step), so the corpus exercises the empty case: a fresh company has no documents, so rows is []. The subset harness compares scalar fields (TS uses ===, so it cannot deep-compare the empty array), hence we assert the deterministic derived companyId — this proves both dispatchers implement the command and key the DTO by the scoped company. Per-row correctness (period fields, canonical ★) is pinned by the Rust unit tests in commands/report_documents_view.rs and the TS mock scenario tests.

journeys.name: history sweep starts a manual sweep and reports empty progress (ADR 0077 T3.2)
journeys._comment: A history sweep enqueues extraction runs; run_history_sweep gates on mode != off (the UI disables the button in mode off), so the corpus opts the company into assist first. Report documents are seeded only through the network-bound fetch/backfill path (same rationale as the T2.1 coverage step), so the sweep runs over an empty company: it enqueues nothing, leaving runsTotal/runsDone/runsFailed at 0 — the stable scalars the subset harness pins. The returned sweep's trigger is the deterministic 'manual'. Per-run progress correctness is pinned by the Rust unit tests in commands/history_sweep.rs and the TS mock scenario tests.

journeys.name: version-aware re-extraction starts a batch and reports empty progress (epic #398 Item B)
journeys._comment: A re-extraction batch selects the company's successful ESEF-tier runs with a stale stored pipeline version and re-arms them; unlike the history sweep it is NOT gated on automation mode (it reprocesses already-stored documents on explicit user request, the same posture as the per-period 'Try again' action). Report documents/runs are seeded only through the network-bound path, so the batch runs over an empty company: it finds zero candidates, leaving runsTotal/runsDone/runsFailed at 0. Candidate-selection correctness is pinned by the Rust unit tests in jobs/pipeline_reextraction.rs and the TS mock scenario tests.

journeys.name: raw tagged-fact coverage + uncrosswalked concepts read empty for a fresh company (ADR 0100, epic #398)
journeys._comment: Layer 1 rows are seeded only through the (unmodeled) extraction pipeline, never a command, so a fresh company reads the empty state on both. Per-row/per-bucket correctness (the projection re-derivation, the promotion write) is pinned by the Rust storage/command unit tests.

journeys.name: decision journal create + list + kind filter (ADR 0071 J2)
journeys._comment: Decision entries are immutable, per-company judgments (ADR 0071). Seed-free: create a company, record a buy, assert it lists, then assert the kind filter excludes it. Ordering (decided_at, not created_at) is pinned by the Rust storage tests; this corpus proves both dispatchers implement create/list + the kind filter and key entries by the scoped company.

journeys.name: short positions read: empty register view (v0.55 T4b, ADR 0069 dec 3)
journeys._comment: The KNF short-selling register is populated by the daily adapter, not a user command, so there is no seed command in the corpus. A tracked company with no register presence reads back the empty view identically on both dispatchers (no active positions, no remembered exit). lastExit:null is the shape-agreeing scalar assertion (serde_json/JS both compare null cleanly; numeric 0.0-vs-0 would diverge). Populated aggregate/delta/ordering math is pinned by the Rust storage tests + the Vitest panel test.

journeys.name: report expectation create + update + list + review + resolution (ADR 0071 J2)
journeys._comment: Pre-report expectations are keyed by (company, event_key) occurrence (ADR 0071). Seed-free: create a company, record a stance + one metric, edit it while unfrozen, list it, read the expectation-vs-actual review, then record the user's own verdict. No facts are seeded, so factsAvailable is false on both sides and the per-metric outcome is unknown. The freeze-on-facts behavior and per-metric met/missed/unknown correctness are pinned by the Rust storage tests; this corpus proves both dispatchers implement all five expectation commands and key by the scoped occurrence.

journeys.name: mcp auth token status + regenerate + revoke lifecycle (ADR 0078 M1)
journeys._comment: The MCP bearer token journeys drive the SAME composed production wrappers (ADR 0099: rotate/revoke restart the listener from stored-credential truth, and regenerate enforces the read-back==plaintext rule), pointed at the persistent rotation-test descriptors whose in-memory backend gives coherent read-back on every platform. EntryOnly keyring truthfulness is pinned separately by the credentials.rs unit tests on the real-keyring scratch slot. Token semantics (64 lowercase hex, unique per call, plaintext returned exactly once, never logged) are pinned by the Rust unit tests in commands/mcp.rs. Both replayers scrub BRAWLER_MCP_TOKEN before this journey per the scrub-hermeticity rule (docs/testing.md).

journeys.name: mcp kpi_acquisition token status + regenerate + revoke lifecycle (ADR 0099 dec. 2)
journeys._comment: The acquisition credential mirrors the primary's lifecycle through the same composed production wrappers on its own rotation-test descriptor (distinct secretKind kpi_acquisition_token). Starts with revoke so the process-global in-memory rotation slot never leaks state across journeys. Both replayers scrub the env fallbacks first (docs/testing.md).

journeys.name: mcp server lifecycle: disabled + enabled-without-token both report not running (ADR 0078 M3)
journeys._comment: The MCP server refuses to run without a keychain token and when the setting is off; both are clean refusals, never crashes (ADR 0078 decision 4). Both replayers scrub BRAWLER_MCP_TOKEN (dev env fallback) before this journey per the scrub-hermeticity rule (docs/testing.md), so no ambient dev token flips the assertion. Rust replayer: set_mcp_enabled drives the real McpLifecycle against an in-memory AppState + the TEST keychain descriptor; with the env scrubbed there is no token, so the enabled path refuses (running:false) and no socket is bound — this keeps the corpus deterministic AND portable across keychain backends (a real ephemeral listener would need a readable token, which the EntryOnly Linux mock backend cannot provide). Mock: running mirrors settings.mcp.enabled AND ctx.mcpToken (null here), so both paths yield running:false. The running-with-a-real-socket path is covered by the Rust nextest lifecycle tests (mcp/lifecycle.rs), which inject a token via the dev env fallback. Only running/port are asserted — error text differs across replayers by design.

journeys.name: a terminally failed background job surfaces as a system attention event (epic #40 S3, ADR 0091 dec. 1)
journeys._comment: The generic failure surface: a job whose retries are exhausted raises a SYSTEM event (no rule) whose evidence is the job row itself. `record_job_failure` is the corpus-only setup bridge for the queue's single terminal-failure point (there is no user command to mint one), mirroring `evaluate_autopilot_completion`. Both sides must agree that the event carries the raw job kind as its detail and the handler's failure subject as its statement, is Notable for every kind, is company-less when the work is workspace-wide (nullable since migration 0118), and answers seen/dismiss like any other event.

ownership overview reads the empty state and set-type is a no-op keyed by company (v0.56 T6, ADR 0072)
journeys._comment: Ownership stakes are written only through the network/report-extraction path (same rationale as the T2.1 coverage step), so the corpus exercises the seed-free empty case: a fresh company has no disclosed stakes, so the overview reads back freeFloatPct '100' with empty holders. expectField pins the deterministic derived companyId (company_gpw_<ticker>, identical on both sides) plus the always-present freeFloatPct scalar. set_ownership_holder_type on a holder that does not exist, and the T8 OCR confirm/reject on a report_document_id with no proposal, all affect zero rows on the Rust side and mutate nothing in the mock, so both dispatchers return the SAME empty overview — proving each implements get + set + the OCR confirm/reject commands and keys the DTO by the scoped company. Populated donut/history/proposal/residual/ocrProposals correctness is pinned by the Rust unit tests in commands/ownership.rs and jobs/ownership_ocr_extraction.rs, the shared populated wire-contract fixture, and the TS OwnershipSection tests.

journeys.name: company health reads the empty state for a fresh company (v0.57 T2, ADR 0083)
journeys._comment: Financial facts land only through the network/extraction path, so the corpus exercises the seed-free empty case: a fresh company has no FY periods, so the health read model reads back an empty history and no latest scores. expectField pins the deterministic derived companyId (company_gpw_<ticker>, identical on both sides), the always-present statement_type default ('industrial'), and the citation labels that always ship with the scores. Populated F/Z correctness is pinned by the Rust unit + golden tests in fundamentals/health and the TS QualityPanel tests.

steps._comment: Insider overview (v0.57 T6, ADR 0083 D7): a fresh company has no parsed insider substrate, so both sides return the empty overview (empty transactions/holdings; both windows belowMinimum count 0). The transactions/holdings arrays are empty, so structural equality is asserted by parity-of-execution; expectField pins only the scalar companyId. No wall-clock field is serialized, so the dual execution stays deterministic.

Red flags (v0.57 T7, ADR 0083 D8): a fresh company has no detections, so both sides return the empty computed view (active + history are empty arrays — asserted by parity-of-execution, not expectField, since === cannot match empty arrays). acknowledge_red_flag on a non-present flag id is idempotent and returns the same empty view on both sides.

Analyst recommendations (v0.58 A3, ADR 0073): a fresh company has no ingested recommendations, so both sides return the empty view (empty entries array — parity-of-execution; latestTarget + lastRefreshedAt omitted because the adapter never ran). expectField pins the scalar companyId.

journeys.name: financial fact annotation set, kept and cleared (#156)
journeys._comment: The one-off '*' annotation is user-authored fact state: create carries it (empty normalizes to null), update keeps it when the field is absent, replaces it with text, and clears it on an empty string. Pinned dual-execution so the mock's keep/clear/replace semantics cannot drift from storage.
